lessons.title: Singleton Pattern
lessons.content: Kotlin's object keyword is a built-in, idiomatic Singleton, lazily and thread-safely instantiated. Real scenario: a single shared analytics client used app-wide.

lessons.title: Factory Pattern
lessons.content: A factory function centralizes object creation logic, hiding construction complexity. Real scenario: a factory choosing between GitHub-JSON vs Firestore repository implementations based on config.

lessons.title: Builder Pattern
lessons.content: Named/default arguments and DSL lambdas largely replace the classic Java Builder pattern. Real scenario: a RequestBuilder DSL configuring a network request declaratively.

codeSnippets.code: fun createUser(name: String, age: Int = 18, isAdmin: Boolean = false) = User(name, age, isAdmin)

lessons.title: Repository Pattern
lessons.content: Abstracts data access behind an interface so callers don't know or care where data comes from. Real scenario: your LessonRepository interface, swappable via a single Hilt @Binds line.

lessons.title: Strategy Pattern
lessons.content: Defines interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface, selected at runtime - often just a function type in Kotlin. Real scenario: swapping sorting strategies for a lesson list via a comparator function.

codeSnippets.code: val sortByOrder: (List<Lesson>) -> List<Lesson> = { it.sortedBy { l -> l.order } }

lessons.title: Observer Pattern
lessons.content: Lets observers react to a subject's state changes - in modern Kotlin, Flow (StateFlow/SharedFlow) IS the idiomatic implementation. Real scenario: your StateFlow<HomeUiState> observed via collectAsState().

lessons.title: Decorator Pattern
lessons.content: Adds behavior by wrapping an object implementing the same interface - Kotlin's 'by' delegation makes this nearly boilerplate-free. Real scenario: wrapping a base Repository with a CachingRepository decorator.

codeSnippets.code: class CachingRepository(private val base: LessonRepository) : LessonRepository by base

lessons.title: Adapter Pattern
lessons.content: Converts one interface into another that client code expects. Real scenario: your LessonEntity.toDomain() mapping functions act as adapters between data-layer and domain-layer shapes.

codeSnippets.code: private fun LessonEntity.toDomain(): Lesson = Lesson(id = id, title = title, content = content)

lessons.title: Command Pattern
lessons.content: Encapsulates a request as an object or, in Kotlin, often just a function reference. Real scenario: pending sync operations represented as command lambdas, executed in sequence.

codeSnippets.code:
val pendingCommands = mutableListOf<suspend () -> Unit>()
pendingCommands.add { repository.syncContent() }

lessons.title: State Pattern
lessons.content: Lets an object change behavior when its internal state changes - sealed classes/interfaces with when are the idiomatic Kotlin implementation. Real scenario: your sealed HomeUiState directly applies this pattern.

lessons.title: Dependency Injection Pattern
lessons.content: Provides an object's dependencies from outside rather than having it construct them itself, improving testability. Real scenario: your Hilt setup constructor-injecting LessonRepository into ViewModels.

codeSnippets.code:
@HiltViewModel
class HomeViewModel @Inject constructor(private val repository: LessonRepository) : ViewModel()
